title: Bill filing opens today for the 90th Texas Legislature — what Webb County should watch
excerpt: Starting today, Texas lawmakers can begin filing bills for the 90th Legislature, which convenes January 12, 2027. Webb Watch 956 will track every filing that touches Webb County.
content:
Starting today, Monday, November 9, Texas lawmakers and lawmakers-elect can begin filing bills for the 90th Texas Legislature, the Texas Legislative Council confirms. The regular session convenes at noon on Tuesday, January 12, 2027.

Prefiling in Texas opens on the first Monday after the general election in even-numbered years, under House Rule 8, Section 7 and Senate Rule 7.04(a). Bills filed now go on the public record through Texas Legislature Online, where anyone can read them for free — long before the session gavels in.

The filing window runs until March 12, 2027, the 60th-day deadline for unrestricted bill filing. The 140-day regular session ends May 31, 2027, known as sine die. The lieutenant governor and the House speaker traditionally reserve the first 20 to 30 bill numbers in each chamber for their priority measures.

Prefiling day is typically a flood: in the last cycle, 1,511 bills and resolutions were filed on the very first day, according to an analysis of the filing data. Webb Watch 956 will be watching today's filings for measures affecting Webb County.

What Webb County should watch

Water. Laredo's water future — supply, reuse and infrastructure funding — has been a standing local issue, and the city has studied wastewater reuse as one option. Any bill touching state water funding or Rio Grande management lands directly on Laredo.

The border and trade. Laredo is the nation's busiest inland port. Bills affecting ports of entry, bridge funding, trade corridors and state border spending matter here more than almost anywhere else in Texas.

Schools. United ISD and Laredo ISD serve tens of thousands of Webb County students. School finance, teacher pay and accountability measures filed in the coming weeks will shape both districts' budgets.

Data centers. The governor's pause on new data-center permits — and whether it is a real pause — was already a live question this fall. Watch for bills that set the rules for large power and water users.

Questions Webb Watch is asking

Which Webb County lawmakers file first, and on what? What do the early filings say about the priorities of the new governor-elect, Gina Hinojosa — who grew up in Brownsville, on the border — and the new Legislature? And which local governments, school districts and community groups in Webb County will weigh in before the session starts?

Nothing has been filed for the 90th session yet as of this morning's opening — the record starts today. Webb Watch 956 will track the filings that matter to Webb County and report what they would actually do, not just what their titles promise.

Update — November 9, 2026 (afternoon)

About 340 bills were filed in the first two hours after filing opened at 8 a.m. Monday, and nearly 970 by noon, according to reports tracking the filings.

First out of the gate were companion bills to expand Medicaid: State Rep. John Bucy filed the House measure, and State Sen. Judith Zaffirini of Laredo filed the Senate version, directing the Texas Health and Human Services Commission to expand the program and submit a plan to federal officials.

Other early filings would raise the state minimum wage, end tax breaks that have drawn data centers to Texas, undo the state law requiring county sheriffs to partner with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and forbid construction of the border wall on state park land, according to the reports.

Bill filing continues through March 12, 2027. Webb Watch 956 will keep tracking the filings that affect Webb County.
